# Introduction
Welcome to the AccuRanker REST API. This API allows you to retrieve metrics about elements like keyword ranks, domains, landing pages, etc. from your AccuRanker account.

# Write API
To create or update elements (groups, domains, or keywords) refer to the [Write API](/api/write-docs).

# Getting started
The first thing to get started with the AccuRanker API is to determine how you will [authenticate](/api/read-docs#section/Authentication) with the API.
Once your authentication method of choice has been chosen you can make your first request.

The following examples will use Python but the methodology can be applied to any programming language.

## Before we begin
The first thing to note is the `fields` query parameter. This is inspired by how GraphQL queries are done, but is essentially a schema you specify for the API to determine which fields to return.

So with `fields` set to `name,address.street,address.country,age,gender` (note how it uses dot notation) the API would return an object (or array of objects) like this:

```javascript
{
    "name": "John Doe",
    "address": {
        "street": "Main St 123",
        "country": "DK",
    },
    "age": 23,
    "gender": "MALE",
}
```

This makes it easy to explicitly tell the API what fields you need and your will always from the parameter know the structure of the data.

## Limitations
- 100 request per min
- Not more then 4 simultaneous connections from the same IP

## Simple request
The following shows a code example of how a simple request, to list all your domains, would look like. Note that we specify the schema in the `fields` query parameter.
> If you do not specify the `fields` query parameter then your responses are going to be empty.

```python
import requests
headers = {'Authorization': f'Token {api_token}'}
url = 'https://app.accuranker.com/api/v4/domains/'

params = {
    'fields': 'id,domain',
}

r = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)

for domain in r.json():
    # ... insert your code here to handle the domain
```

## Advanced request
Now lets try to get some historic data, by selecting the fields within `ranks`, as explained [here](/api/read-docs#section/Using-fields).

```python
import requests
headers = {'Authorization': f'Token {api_token}'}
url = 'https://app.accuranker.com/api/v4/domains/{domain_id}/keywords/'

params = {
    'fields': 'id,keyword,ranks.rank,ranks.created_at',
}

r = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)

for keyword in r.json():
    # ... insert your code here to handle the keyword

    for rank in keyword['ranks']:
        # ... insert your code here to handle the rank

```

## Advanced request with period
We can set the desired period using the `period_from` and `period_to` query parameters, as explained [here](/api/read-docs#section/Using-period).

```python
import requests
headers = {'Authorization': f'Token {api_token}'}
url = 'https://app.accuranker.com/api/v4/domains/{domain_id}/keywords/'

params = {
    'fields': 'id,keyword,ranks.rank,ranks.created_at,competitor_ranks.rank,competitor_ranks.created_at,competitor_ranks.competitor.domain',
    'period_from': '2025-05-17',
    'period_to': '2025-05-24',
}

r = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)

for keyword in r.json():
    # ... insert your code here to handle the keyword

    for rank in keyword['ranks']:
        # ... insert your code here to handle the rank

    for competitor_rank in keyword['competitor_ranks']:
        # ... insert your code here to handle the competitor
```


## Advanced request with API filter
Finally we can use an API filter to filter the data we return using `filter_id` in query parameters, as explained [here](/api/read-docs#section/Using-filter).
This is especially nice if we only want mobile rankings, only keywords ranking 1-10 or really anything else. You can find your API filters [here](/app/integrations/api).

```python
import requests
headers = {'Authorization': f'Token {api_token}'}
url = 'https://app.accuranker.com/api/v4/domains/{domain_id}/keywords/'

params = {
    'fields': 'id,keyword,ranks.rank,ranks.created_at,competitor_ranks.rank,competitor_ranks.created_at,competitor_ranks.competitor.domain',
    'filter_id': 1,
    'period_from': '2018-05-17',
    'period_to': '2018-05-24',
}

r = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)

for keyword in r.json():
    # ... insert your code here to handle the keyword

    for rank in keyword['ranks']:
        # ... insert your code here to handle the rank

    for competitor_rank in keyword['competitor_ranks']:
        # ... insert your code here to handle the competitor
```


# Errors
The API uses standard HTTP status codes to indicate the success or failure of the API call. The body of the response will be JSON in the following format:

```javascript
{
    "detail": "Not found."
}
```


# Authentication
All requests must be authenticated using a token or OAuth.
If you are creating an API integration that only you will use, we recommend using token authentication - it is the easiest.
However, if you are creating an integration that other users might use, we recommend using OAuth2.

## Token
You can find your API token [here](/app/profile).
Once you have the token, it should be added as an `Authorization` header with the prefix `Token`.

```
Authorization: Token YOUR_API_TOKEN
```

## OAuth
First of all, you need to create an AccuRanker OAuth application [here](/oauth/applications/).
You can start the authentication flow when you have your app's `Client ID` and `Client Secret`.
The first thing you need to do is to get your `Authorization code`, or whatever means you use to authorize the app.

Next, the code must to be exchanged for an `Access Token`. With a request like the example just below.
You may need to change the value for grant_type with a request like the example below:

 ```
 curl -X POST \
    -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
    "https://app.accuranker.com/oauth/token/" \
    -d "grant_type=authorization_code" \
    -d "client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET" \
    -d "client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID" \
    -d "code=YOUR_CODE"
 ```
If successful the request will return access and a refresh token in the response. Like this:

```
{
  "access_token": YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN,
  "expires_in": 36000,
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "scope": "read",
  "refresh_token": {refresh_token}"
}
```

The access token should be added as an `Authorization` header with the prefix `Bearer` when you have the access token.
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
```
### Refreshing the access token
If your Access Token has expired, you can refresh it using the Refresh Token. The request should look like this:

```
 curl -X POST \
    -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
    "https://app.accuranker.com/oauth/token/" \
    -d "grant_type=refresh_token" \
    -d "refresh_token=YOUR_REFRESH_TOKEN"
```

### Authorization from other accounts
To authorise the application from other accounts, you need to generate a special authorization_code. Create a link like this:
```
https://app.accuranker.com/oauth/authorize/?client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI&state=YOUR_STATE&response_type=code
```
where

| Parameter      | Description                                        |
| ---------------- |--------------------------------------------|
| client_id         | The id of your application (found [here](/oauth/applications/)) |
| redirect_uri      | The redirect URI of your application (found [here](/oauth/applications/))|
| state             | Optional parameter that gets passed through the flow.|

and give it to a user of the account you want access to.

# Using fields
The AccuRanker API uses fields to determine what information it should return. So for each request you should parse the `fields` query parameter to explicitly tell the server what fields to return in the JSON response.

> `fields` uses dot notation. So should you need fields on an underlying child object, simply dot your way to the field. (see example 2)

## Examples

**Example 1**
We wish to retrieve the `domain` and `display_name` fields on the `/domains/{id}/` endpoint.

```
/domains/{id}/?fields=domain,display_name
```

# Using period/filter
Some request allows you to parse `period_from` and `period_to` as query parameters. This will allow the server to serve the historic numbers from the given period.
You must specify both parameters to override the default* behavior.

> `period_from` and `period_to` expects a date in the format `YYYY-MM-DD` and they are inclusive.

**Please note:** There is currently a limit of maximum 100 days when using the period parameters.

(*) Default behavior: When not both `period_from` and `period_to` are defined, we will return historical data from the latest day all keywords on the domain(s)
was fully refreshed. That would usually be today or yesterday.

## Examples

**Example 1**
We wish to get the ranks for the first week of the year.

```
/domains/{id}/keywords/?fields=keyword,ranks.rank,ranks.created_at&period_from=2018-01-01&period_to=2018-01-07
```

**Example 2**
We wish to get the domain share of voice for 5 specific days.

```
/domains/{id}/?fields=domain,history.date,history.share_of_voice&period_from=2018-12-20&period_to=2018-12-24
```

# Using saved filters/segments
Some requests allow you to pass `filter_id` in query parameters. This allows the server to filter the data using a saved filter/segment (in the same way that you can use filters/segments within AccuRanker).

## How do I create an API filter?

1. Create a normal segment (read more about this [here](https://www.accuranker.com/help/keywords/filtering-keywords)) and save it.
3. Edit the saved segment and mark it as an API filter.
4. Save your new API filter and view the existing ones [here](/app/integrations/api).

## Examples

**Example 1**
We have set up an API filter that only show mobile rankings.

```
/domains/{id}/keywords/?fields=keyword,ranks.rank,ranks.created_at&filter_id=1
```

**Example 2**
We have set up a filter that only shows keywords ranked 1-10

```
/domains/{id}/?fields=domain,history.date,history.share_of_voice&filter_id=654
```

# Using dynamic filters
For more dynamic filtering needs, you can use the dynamic filters that also powers the filter system in the application. Filters can be nested and combined with AND/OR logic, and you can choose from a wide variety of comparators to create the perfect filter for your use case, learn more in the examples below.
You can send filters directly in the request body using POST instead of GET.  This is useful when filters are too complex for URL query parameters or when you want to avoid URL length limitations. It is however also possible to specify filters through query parameters.


## Filter format
The request body should contain a JSON object with the following structure:

```json
{
    "filters": [
        {"name": "rank", "comparator": "lt", "value": 10},
        {"name": "keyword", "comparator": "contains", "value": "seo"}
    ],
    "operator": "and"
}
```

## Available comparators

| Comparator | Description |
|---|---|
| `eq` | Equal to |
| `ne` | Not equal to |
| `gt` | Greater than |
| `gte` | Greater than or equal to |
| `lt` | Less than |
| `lte` | Less than or equal to |
| `between` | Between two values (inclusive), expects an array of two values |
| `contains` | Contains substring |
| `not_contains` | Does not contain substring |
| `starts_with` | Starts with substring |
| `ends_with` | Ends with substring |
| `regex` | Matches regular expression (Google RE2 syntax; no PCRE lookarounds or backreferences) |
| `not_regex` | Does not match regular expression (Google RE2 syntax; no PCRE lookarounds or backreferences) |
| `any` | Matches any of the provided values |
| `all` | Matches all of the provided values |
| `none` | Matches none of the provided values |
| `empty` | Value is empty or not set |

## Examples

**Example 1**
Get keywords with rank between 1 and 10:

```python
import requests
headers = {'Authorization': f'Token {api_token}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
url = 'https://app.accuranker.com/api/v4/domains/{domain_id}/keywords/?fields=id,keyword,ranks.rank'

data = {
    "filters": [
        {"name": "rank", "comparator": "between", "value": [1, 10]}
    ],
    "operator": "and"
}

r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=data)
```

**Example 2**
Get keywords containing "seo" with search volume > 1000:

```python
data = {
    "filters": [
        {"name": "keyword", "comparator": "contains", "value": "seo"},
        {"name": "search_volume", "comparator": "gt", "value": 1000}
    ],
    "operator": "and"
}

r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=data)
```

**Example 3**
Using nested filters with OR logic - get keywords that contains SEO and are rank 1-3 OR have search volume > 10000:

```python
data = {
    "filters": [
        {
            "operator": "or",
            "filters": [
                {"name": "rank", "comparator": "between", "value": [1, 3]},
                {"name": "search_volume", "comparator": "gt", "value": 10000}
            ]
        },
        {"name": "keyword", "comparator": "contains", "value": "seo"}
    ],
    "operator": "and"
}

r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=data)
```

This example returns keywords containing "seo" that ALSO match either condition: rank between 1-3 OR search volume > 10000.

comparison.title: Comparison
comparison.description:
Depended on the type:
* string: `contains`, `not_contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `eq` and `ne`
* num: `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `eq` and `between`
* array: `any`, `all` and `none`
* list: `contains`
* bool: `eq` and  `ne`
* datetime: `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `eq` and `between`

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: This endpoint allows you to retrieve data related to your account and sub-accounts with an active plan with API enabled.

tags.name: Prompts
tags.description:
This endpoint allows you to retrieve data relating to your prompt(s) and prompt(s) ranking(s), as well as the competitor(s) for each prompt.

**This endpoint has restricted access**, you will need to have an AccuLLM plan with API access enabled. If you're interested contact the support.

**results** (*uses `period_from` and `period_to`*):
Ranks for the prompt for you and your competitors.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description:
This endpoint allows you to retrieve data relating to your domain(s) and the history of the domain(s), as well as the competitor(s) for each domain and their history.

**history** (*uses `period_from` and `period_to`*):
Historical information for the domain, grouped by date.

**competitors**:
The competitors for the domain.

**competitors[n].history** (*uses `period_from` and `period_to`*):
Historical information for the competitor grouped by date.

tags.name: Keywords
tags.description:
This endpoint allows you to retrieve data relating to your keyword(s) and keyword(s) ranking(s), as well as the competitor(s) for each keyword.

**ranks** (*uses `period_from` and `period_to`*):
Ranks for the keyword. Note that the `id` field for ranks and SERP features is always `0` because they are legacy fields that are still available for backward compatibility.

**initial_rank**:
Initial rank for the keyword when first added to AccuRanker. See note about the `id` field above.

**competitor_ranks** (*uses `period_from` and `period_to`*):
Competitor ranks for the keyword.

**search_volume.history** (*DOES NOT take `period_from` and `period_to` into consideration*):
Historic search volume up to four years back for the keyword.

tags.name: Serps
tags.description:
This endpoint allows you to retrieve the HTML related to the Search engine results page for a given keyword at a given date.

You can find all ranks associated with a keyword in the Keywords endpoint in the ranks field.

**This endpoint has restricted access**, if you're interested contact the support.

tags.name: Landing Pages
tags.description:
This endpoint allows you to retrieve data related to your landing page(s) and their history.

**history** (*uses `period_from` and `period_to`*):
Historical information for the landing page, grouped by date.

**history.ga4**: If you have connected your Google Analytics 4 account to AccuRanker,
you can pull analytics data related to your landing page(s) like this `/domains/{id}/landing_pages/?fields=path,history.date,history.ga4`.
Check out the sample response to the right for the current fields available and contact our support team if you have any questions.
Be aware that when you retrieve data for today, we most likely won't have any GA4 data yet - as the day hasn't ended yet.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description:
This endpoint allows you to retrieve data about your tags and their history. You can find aggregated data for both your dynamic tags and regular tags.

**history** (*uses `period_from` and `period_to`*):
Historical information for the tag, grouped by date.
